The proposed shape follows from that: light the door for everyone first, then crown Teachers and the Numbers-narrative professions with deeply designed toolkits, hand Engineers their near-free one, and let the user make the two taste calls the evidence narrows but cannot decide.

content.value: The wish, the frame, and how the investigation ran

content.value: The finding that reorders everything
The engine kept growing; the door never did. Twelve S-tier blocks merged in one wave — and not one was added to the menu a human can see.

Every lane hit the same wall from a different direction, and the storm's editor census made it exact (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit carries the full census). The union of every human insert mechanism in the Studio editor — the 33-entry slash menu, the 25-type add-block dropdown, the 23-type canvas allowlist, the command palette — is exactly 33 of 75 classified block types. Not one instrument block is reachable: chart, stat, heatmap, form, questionnaire, sheet, and equation all have no insert path. The equation block shipped S-tier at usefulness 4.60 with three byte-identical surface twins and golden parity — and a mathematician cannot create one from the editor at all. Its graded source-textarea editor was never delivered either (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting).

This converts the corpus's most alarming number — 77.6% of 22,701 production blocks are bare paragraph + heading — from a demand signal into a supply artifact. The engine's own users, agents included, never reached the rich vocabulary because nothing offered it. The data-analyst notebook exists end-to-end today (sheet embed, live charts, write-through refresh) and has been used twice, ever. The anonymous form endpoint is live in prod with one real response — and the reader renders its form with no submit button, a door with no handle by explicit design (PR #5653 deferred the reader UI). The one-call playground that provisions a workspace, token, and seeded showcase Paper sits fully built behind a single require_admin flag, returning 401 to every stranger.

Three delivery-debt beliefs died under evidence along the way: the reader-CSS debt is PAID (PR #5651 shipped styling for all 18 previously-unstyled families); the TUI is NOT the weak parity leg (all 75 types have dedicated Go renderers — email is the constrained surface); and all 12 S-tier wishlist blocks are DONE. What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps — plus two verticals whose toolkits are ~90% shipped without anyone having assembled them, and the known capability gaps (math typesetting depth, citations, chart statistics, music) that sit exactly where professional cravings live.

The expensive half of a professional product — a parity-locked multi-surface render engine, a formula engine, live data plumbing, template locks, an anonymous intake endpoint — is built and CI-gated. The missing half is registry entries, default clauses, designed presets, starter templates, one controller branch, and one router pipeline. The cheapest wave in the whole program is also the one that serves all twelve professions at once, and it doubles as the falsifiable demand test: if lighting the door doesn't move usage, re-examine before building deeper (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms, Move 0).

content.value: A Paper crosses into PHI/special-category territory the instant a form collects any of the 18 HIPAA identifiers tied to one person for a clinical purpose (45 CFR §160.103 + the BAA requirement). A US teacher's NAMED gradebook on a personal account fails FERPA's direct-control test — while fully anonymous submissions fall outside FERPA entirely, which makes the already-anonymous form endpoint the legally correct default, not just a convenience. EU health data needs a GDPR Art. 9 basis plus an Art. 28 DPA. Solo lawyers are ALLOWED with reasonable-efforts diligence. Product consequence: ship anonymous, aggregate, no-PII shapes by default; any named-intake or consent template ships explicitly flagged as collecting regulated data; a real BAA/DPA program is a business decision that PRECEDES those templates. Full matrix with controlling rules: papers-pro-toolkit-profession-atlas.

The proposed shape — two layers, three crowns, four spines

Build in two layers. LAYER A — one wave, serves all twelve professions: light the authoring door (palette 33→60 with designed presets and pickers, server default parity, compound-insert starters, the equation authoring rescue, markdown import wired to ingest, vertical doc-type templates on the proven pdd-t1 lock, a decided browser-print v1, and the one-flag anonymous playground). content.value: Doctrine rulings
Three questions no lane could settle alone were flagged to this capstone. Two are ruled here with reasoning; one is consolidated into a single user gate.

The question, asked identically by three lanes: must every surface render from source, or may the server pre-resolve (citation formatting, numbering, freshness stamps, notation snapshots)? RULING: the server MAY pre-resolve, and derived document-level content SHOULD flow through one canonical Elixir resolver — because the system already does exactly this, safely, at scale. TaskResolver's resolve/2 + preview/2 split serves all six render call sites (web reader, live re-resolve, email snapshot-at-send, source endpoint, ?resolve= for the TUI, Studio preview) and never persists a resolved row; stored blocks stay byte-stable source, which is what the canvas diff and the golden harness actually require. The law is a two-line rule: SOURCE-level rendering (an equation's glyphs, a chord line, a chart's pixels) = three surface twins, byte-identical grammar. DOCUMENT-level derivation (bibliography text, assigned numbers, resolved labels, as-of stamps) = ONE resolver, all surfaces consume its output. Consequences: the apparatus pass is a new resolver in TaskResolver's shape; the CSL formatter is written once in Elixir (not three twins); freshness stamps are resolver chrome and legal; equation grammar v2 stays three-twin because equations render from source on every surface. This halves the evidence spine's cost and makes numbering byte-stable across email, TUI, and exports by construction.

items.value: Demand is inferred, not measured.

All internal usage data is agent-authored; no human professional has ever been watched authoring a Paper. The crowns rest deliberately on external market evidence (TpT, the re-export loop, the Confluence exodus). Wave 1 is the cheap falsifiable test, and the flagship showcase Papers should double as the first instrumented measurement.
The teacher wedge must beat free.

Google Forms is $0, district-mandated, and still improving (native close/caps landed Jan 2026 — demoted provenance, verify before scoping stage 6 against it). The wedge survives on what Forms cannot be: a beautiful printed artifact and a live form as ONE document, FERPA-safe by anonymity. This remains the least-grounded switching estimate in the program.
Feature-parity slippage is proven, not hypothetical.

Chart annotations shipped web-only despite the type-parity gate — the gate locks types, not features. Every chart/form feature in waves 2-3 lands as a three-surface set with per-surface goldens, or the surfaces fork.
The parity treadmill on notation.

Hand-growing a bounded TeX parser across three twins toward LaTeX-grade is parity-fragile. Mitigations: Temml as a frozen reference spec, golden parity at birth, and a hard scope line at the problem-set minimal set — beyond it, the honest answer is Rung 3's engine, not a bigger macro table.
Each new aggregate source re-opens privacy design.
k-anon, measure whitelist, and tenancy checks were task-shaped by construction. form_responses is the easiest first source but still needs its own k-anonymity story.
The pitch must stay honest.

'Live' = refresh-on-save, not reader-side recompute; version history is professional-grade, never 'compliance'; email math stays a badge until the derived-asset gate opens. The quality-bar thesis dies the moment marketing outruns the render.
Concurrent-session hazard.

The working tree provably lags origin/main; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic re-verifies the 33, the open task states, and PR-level facts at wave start — this repo moves daily.
Where does the individual professional permanently live?

Playground workspaces carry a 48h TTL; the free cloud trial reaches a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the playground flag is cheap; deciding the durable home (TTL'd playground → claim? free papers-only tier? paid instance?) is a product decision outside this repo — without it, the toolkits polish a door with no house behind it.

content.value: The recommendation

The verdict is GO, with the two-layer shape rather than the wish's implicit build-blocks-per-profession shape. The evidence is unambiguous that the highest-leverage first wave is the door, not any new capability: it is the cheap half, it serves all twelve professions simultaneously, it has zero doctrine questions, and it falsifiably tests demand before the deeper waves spend. Then crown Teachers (wave 2) and Numbers-narrative (wave 3, engineers' template pack alongside), then the user-decided deep third crown (wave 4) whose evidence spine — the apparatus pass — serves lawyers and mathematicians regardless of the call. Run it as epic cycles per the standing rule; each wave above is one cycle with its charter drawn from this report and its lane Paper.

content.value: The finding that reorders everything
The engine kept growing; the door never did. Twelve S-tier blocks merged in one wave — and not one was added to the menu a human can see.

Every lane hit the same wall from a different direction, and the storm's editor census made it exact (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit carries the full census). The union of every human insert mechanism in the Studio editor — the 33-entry slash menu, the 25-type add-block dropdown, the 23-type canvas allowlist, the command palette — is exactly 33 of 75 classified block types. Not one instrument block is reachable: chart, stat, heatmap, form, questionnaire, sheet, and equation all have no insert path. The equation block shipped S-tier at usefulness 4.60 with three byte-identical surface twins and golden parity — and a mathematician cannot create one from the editor at all. Its graded source-textarea editor was never delivered either (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting).

This converts the corpus's most alarming number — 77.6% of 22,701 production blocks are bare paragraph + heading — from a demand signal into a supply artifact. The engine's own users, agents included, never reached the rich vocabulary because nothing offered it. The data-analyst notebook exists end-to-end today (sheet embed, live charts, write-through refresh) and has been used twice, ever. The anonymous form endpoint is live in prod with one real response — and the reader renders its form with no submit button, a door with no handle by explicit design (PR #5653 deferred the reader UI). The one-call playground that provisions a workspace, token, and seeded showcase Paper sits fully built behind a single require_admin flag, returning 401 to every stranger.

Three delivery-debt beliefs died under evidence along the way: the reader-CSS debt is PAID (PR #5651 shipped styling for all 18 previously-unstyled families); the TUI is NOT the weak parity leg (all 75 types have dedicated Go renderers — email is the constrained surface); and all 12 S-tier wishlist blocks are DONE. What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps — plus two verticals whose toolkits are ~90% shipped without anyone having assembled them, and the known capability gaps (math typesetting depth, citations, chart statistics, music) that sit exactly where professional cravings live.

The expensive half of a professional product — a parity-locked multi-surface render engine, a formula engine, live data plumbing, template locks, an anonymous intake endpoint — is built and CI-gated. The missing half is registry entries, default clauses, designed presets, starter templates, one controller branch, and one router pipeline. The cheapest wave in the whole program is also the one that serves all twelve professions at once, and it doubles as the falsifiable demand test: if lighting the door doesn't move usage, re-examine before building deeper (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms, Move 0).

content.value: A Paper crosses into PHI/special-category territory the instant a form collects any of the 18 HIPAA identifiers tied to one person for a clinical purpose (45 CFR §160.103 + the BAA requirement). content.value: Doctrine rulings
Three questions no lane could settle alone were flagged to this capstone. Two are ruled here with reasoning; one is consolidated into a single user gate.

The question, asked identically by three lanes: must every surface render from source, or may the server pre-resolve (citation formatting, numbering, freshness stamps, notation snapshots)? RULING: the server MAY pre-resolve, and derived document-level content SHOULD flow through one canonical Elixir resolver — because the system already does exactly this, safely, at scale. TaskResolver's resolve/2 + preview/2 split serves all six render call sites (web reader, live re-resolve, email snapshot-at-send, source endpoint, ?resolve= for the TUI, Studio preview) and never persists a resolved row; stored blocks stay byte-stable source, which is what the canvas diff and the golden harness actually require. The law is a two-line rule: SOURCE-level rendering (an equation's glyphs, a chord line, a chart's pixels) = three surface twins, byte-identical grammar. DOCUMENT-level derivation (bibliography text, assigned numbers, resolved labels, as-of stamps) = ONE resolver, all surfaces consume its output. Consequences: the apparatus pass is a new resolver in TaskResolver's shape; the CSL formatter is written once in Elixir (not three twins); freshness stamps are resolver chrome and legal; equation grammar v2 stays three-twin because equations render from source on every surface. This halves the evidence spine's cost and makes numbering byte-stable across email, TUI, and exports by construction.

content.value: Risks and unknowns

items.value: Demand is inferred, not measured.

All internal usage data is agent-authored; no human professional has ever been watched authoring a Paper. The crowns rest deliberately on external market evidence (TpT, the re-export loop, the Confluence exodus). Wave 1 is the cheap falsifiable test, and the flagship showcase Papers should double as the first instrumented measurement.
The teacher wedge must beat free.

Google Forms is $0, district-mandated, and still improving (native close/caps landed Jan 2026 — demoted provenance, verify before scoping stage 6 against it). The wedge survives on what Forms cannot be: a beautiful printed artifact and a live form as ONE document, FERPA-safe by anonymity. This remains the least-grounded switching estimate in the program.
Feature-parity slippage is proven, not hypothetical.

Chart annotations shipped web-only despite the type-parity gate — the gate locks types, not features. Every chart/form feature in waves 2-3 lands as a three-surface set with per-surface goldens, or the surfaces fork.
The parity treadmill on notation.

Hand-growing a bounded TeX parser across three twins toward LaTeX-grade is parity-fragile. Mitigations: Temml as a frozen reference spec, golden parity at birth, and a hard scope line at the problem-set minimal set — beyond it, the honest answer is Rung 3's engine, not a bigger macro table.
Each new aggregate source re-opens privacy design.
k-anon, measure whitelist, and tenancy checks were task-shaped by construction. form_responses is the easiest first source but still needs its own k-anonymity story.
The pitch must stay honest.

'Live' = refresh-on-save, not reader-side recompute; version history is professional-grade, never 'compliance'; email math stays a badge until the derived-asset gate opens. The quality-bar thesis dies the moment marketing outruns the render.
Concurrent-session hazard.

The working tree provably lags origin/main; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic re-verifies the 33, the open task states, and PR-level facts at wave start — this repo moves daily.
Where does the individual professional permanently live?

Playground workspaces carry a 48h TTL; the free cloud trial reaches a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the playground flag is cheap; deciding the durable home (TTL'd playground → claim? free papers-only tier? paid instance?) is a product decision outside this repo — without it, the toolkits polish a door with no house behind it.

content.value: The recommendation

The verdict is GO, with the two-layer shape rather than the wish's implicit build-blocks-per-profession shape. The evidence is unambiguous that the highest-leverage first wave is the door, not any new capability: it is the cheap half, it serves all twelve professions simultaneously, it has zero doctrine questions, and it falsifiably tests demand before the deeper waves spend. Then crown Teachers (wave 2) and Numbers-narrative (wave 3, engineers' template pack alongside), then the user-decided deep third crown (wave 4) whose evidence spine — the apparatus pass — serves lawyers and mathematicians regardless of the call. Run it as epic cycles per the standing rule; each wave above is one cycle with its charter drawn from this report and its lane Paper.

This report stands alone, but every section compresses a lane Paper that holds the full depth: complete profession profiles and the regulatory matrix with controlling rules (papers-pro-toolkit-profession-atlas); the three-rung notation family with per-block attrs shapes, the engine census, and the competitor matrix (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting); the apparatus-pass architecture, the CSL/DOI design, the legal toolkit, and the record-integrity audit with trigger-level evidence (papers-pro-toolkit-evidence-record); the ranked chart-statistics pack, the six-stage form lifecycle, and the insert census (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms); the toolkit anatomy, the interop wall, the sequencing rationale, and the full coverage appendices (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit). Each lane's coverage appendix lists what was checked and NOT found — absences are decisions-in-waiting, and they are this program's sharpest evidence.

What do the twelve professions need from Papers? A door they can walk through (palette, starters, import, playground), instruments that close their own loops (forms that grade, numbers that stay live), an apparatus that makes documents prove things (citations, numbering, records told honestly), notation that respects their craft (equations, chords) — all under one law: every block renders beautifully on web, email, and terminal. The engine is already most of the way there; this program's job is to open the door and set three flagship examples of the quality bar so high that the Papers sell Barkpark by themselves.

Papers for Professionals — the crown report: twelve professions, four spines, and the door that was never opened

Barkpark Papers · deep investigation · THE CROWN REPORT · 2026-07-23

The user asked what musicians, data analysts, healthcare professionals, financial people, lawyers, mathematicians, scientists, industrial and general engineers, dentists, and teachers each need from Papers — and for a toolkit so incredible that people would use Barkpark for Papers alone. Five investigation lanes answered with evidence: a demand atlas over all twelve professions, three capability-spine designs (notation, evidence, living data), and an engine ground-truth study with the crown verdict. This report is their synthesis — one narrative, one argument, every decisive fact kept. The single finding that reorders everything: the engine is not the bottleneck; the door is. Barkpark's Paper engine holds 75 block types on three CI-locked surfaces, an Excel-class formula engine, live query blocks, and a fresh anonymous form endpoint — and a human professional can insert exactly 33 of those 75 types. The proposed shape follows from that: light the door for everyone first, then crown Teachers and the Numbers-narrative professions with deeply designed toolkits, hand Engineers their near-free one, and let the user make the two taste calls the evidence narrows but cannot decide.

The wish, the frame, and how the investigation ran

The wish, verbatim in spirit: map what every named profession craves from Papers — musicians, data analysts, healthcare professionals, financial people, lawyers, mathematicians, scientists, industrial engineers, engineers in general, dentists, teachers — holistically, and build a toolkit so incredible that people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone. The interview pinned four frame-setting truths before the run launched, and every lane inherited them as law:

  • The buyer is an individual professional. A single dentist, teacher, or analyst picks Barkpark for their own documents. Consumer-grade onboarding, zero setup — the Paper IS the product.
  • The portability doctrine holds. Every new need becomes a new portable block type rendering on all three surfaces — web, email, terminal. No web-only escape hatches.
  • Map ALL, then crown 2–3. Every profession gets a profile; two or three highest-leverage verticals get deeply designed toolkits.
  • The quality bar itself is the attraction. In the user's own words: 'no focus on commercial — Papers should be so nice that people get attracted to Barkpark in general because the quality bar is so high.' This is a capability study, not a pricing exercise.

Five lanes cut the problem as a demand-meets-supply matrix: one lane owns every profession's demand so nobody falls through the cracks; three lanes own the capability spines the professions converge on; one lane owns engine ground truth, toolkit anatomy, and the crown verdict. Each published a full preparation Paper — this report takes their best material and stands alone; descend into a lane only for its full depth.

The finding that reorders everything

The engine kept growing; the door never did. Twelve S-tier blocks merged in one wave — and not one was added to the menu a human can see.

Every lane hit the same wall from a different direction, and the storm's editor census made it exact (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit carries the full census). The union of every human insert mechanism in the Studio editor — the 33-entry slash menu, the 25-type add-block dropdown, the 23-type canvas allowlist, the command palette — is exactly 33 of 75 classified block types. Not one instrument block is reachable: chart, stat, heatmap, form, questionnaire, sheet, and equation all have no insert path. The equation block shipped S-tier at usefulness 4.60 with three byte-identical surface twins and golden parity — and a mathematician cannot create one from the editor at all. Its graded source-textarea editor was never delivered either (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting).

This converts the corpus's most alarming number — 77.6% of 22,701 production blocks are bare paragraph + heading — from a demand signal into a supply artifact. The engine's own users, agents included, never reached the rich vocabulary because nothing offered it. The data-analyst notebook exists end-to-end today (sheet embed, live charts, write-through refresh) and has been used twice, ever. The anonymous form endpoint is live in prod with one real response — and the reader renders its form with no submit button, a door with no handle by explicit design (PR #5653 deferred the reader UI). The one-call playground that provisions a workspace, token, and seeded showcase Paper sits fully built behind a single require_admin flag, returning 401 to every stranger.

Three delivery-debt beliefs died under evidence along the way: the reader-CSS debt is PAID (PR #5651 shipped styling for all 18 previously-unstyled families); the TUI is NOT the weak parity leg (all 75 types have dedicated Go renderers — email is the constrained surface); and all 12 S-tier wishlist blocks are DONE. What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps — plus two verticals whose toolkits are ~90% shipped without anyone having assembled them, and the known capability gaps (math typesetting depth, citations, chart statistics, music) that sit exactly where professional cravings live.

Why this is good news
The expensive half of a professional product — a parity-locked multi-surface render engine, a formula engine, live data plumbing, template locks, an anonymous intake endpoint — is built and CI-gated. The missing half is registry entries, default clauses, designed presets, starter templates, one controller branch, and one router pipeline. The cheapest wave in the whole program is also the one that serves all twelve professions at once, and it doubles as the falsifiable demand test: if lighting the door doesn't move usage, re-examine before building deeper (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms, Move 0).

A Barkpark Paper is the only document artifact that is simultaneously: a beautifully printed handout, a byte-exact email, a terminal-rendered document, a live instrument (a form that collects, a chart that refreshes, a sheet that recomputes), and a portable JSON source no vendor holds hostage. The regulatory boundary is per-FIELD, not per-vertical
A Paper crosses into PHI/special-category territory the instant a form collects any of the 18 HIPAA identifiers tied to one person for a clinical purpose (45 CFR §160.103 + the BAA requirement). A US teacher's NAMED gradebook on a personal account fails FERPA's direct-control test — while fully anonymous submissions fall outside FERPA entirely, which makes the already-anonymous form endpoint the legally correct default, not just a convenience. EU health data needs a GDPR Art. 9 basis plus an Art. 28 DPA. Solo lawyers are ALLOWED with reasonable-efforts diligence. Product consequence: ship anonymous, aggregate, no-PII shapes by default; any named-intake or consent template ships explicitly flagged as collecting regulated data; a real BAA/DPA program is a business decision that PRECEDES those templates. Full matrix with controlling rules: papers-pro-toolkit-profession-atlas.

One census caveat the whole program must respect: for five of the twelve professions (financial, lawyers, healthcare, dentists, musicians-as-notation) the dominant template artifact is NOT prose-shaped — it is a spreadsheet model, a fill-in contract, a rigid SOAP form, a score. The proposed shape — two layers, three crowns, four spines

The shape in one paragraph
Build in two layers. LAYER A — one wave, serves all twelve professions: light the authoring door (palette 33→60 with designed presets and pickers, server default parity, compound-insert starters, the equation authoring rescue, markdown import wired to ingest, vertical doc-type templates on the proven pdd-t1 lock, a decided browser-print v1, and the one-flag anonymous playground). LAYER B — one wave per crown: TEACHERS (worksheet/self-grading-quiz/intake toolkit; the transport is live, the market is the strongest that exists), NUMBERS-NARRATIVE analysts + financial (data-notebook and client-report toolkit; the sheets engine is Excel-class today), and ENGINEERS as the near-free toolkit (templates + flagship demos over the already-engineer-shaped vocabulary). The contested DEEP third crown — scientists vs musicians — is priced and left to the user, with the evidence favoring scientists and the musician delight pack shipping cheaply either way.

The wave sequence

  1. Light the door — all twelve at once

    Palette + presets for the locked-out blocks, equation rescue, starters, markdown ingest, browser print, anonymous playground. The falsifiable demand test: if the open door doesn't move usage, re-examine before spending deeper.

  2. Crown Teachers

    Reader submit UI, question types v2, server-side grading — on the transport that shipped this month.

  3. Crown Numbers-narrative (+ Engineers' free pack)

    Chart-statistics floor, annotation parity, sheet-source blocks, CSV import; the engineer template pack rides along.

  4. The taste-call crown

    Scientists (evidence-favored) or Musicians (spectacle-favored) — the user's call; the musician delight pack ships regardless.

Why light-the-door first is not a taste call: the diagnosis is evidence-ordered — discoverability > authoring cost > delivery debt, and the third cause is now fixed, which promotes the first two. The engine:door ratio (75:33) is measured, not felt. 71 drift-spelled list blocks in production prove authors reach for names they cannot discover. And Layer A is registry entries, default clauses, one controller branch, and one router pipeline — no new renderers, no new goldens, no doctrine questions (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit).

Doctrine rulings

Three questions no lane could settle alone were flagged to this capstone. Two are ruled here with reasoning; one is consolidated into a single user gate.

RULING 1 — Resolve-at-render, never-at-rest (the pre-resolve doctrine)
The question, asked identically by three lanes: must every surface render from source, or may the server pre-resolve (citation formatting, numbering, freshness stamps, notation snapshots)? RULING: the server MAY pre-resolve, and derived document-level content SHOULD flow through one canonical Elixir resolver — because the system already does exactly this, safely, at scale. TaskResolver's resolve/2 + preview/2 split serves all six render call sites (web reader, live re-resolve, email snapshot-at-send, source endpoint, ?resolve= for the TUI, Studio preview) and never persists a resolved row; stored blocks stay byte-stable source, which is what the canvas diff and the golden harness actually require. The law is a two-line rule: SOURCE-level rendering (an equation's glyphs, a chord line, a chart's pixels) = three surface twins, byte-identical grammar. DOCUMENT-level derivation (bibliography text, assigned numbers, resolved labels, as-of stamps) = ONE resolver, all surfaces consume its output. Consequences: the apparatus pass is a new resolver in TaskResolver's shape; the CSL formatter is written once in Elixir (not three twins); freshness stamps are resolver chrome and legal; equation grammar v2 stays three-twin because equations render from source on every surface. This halves the evidence spine's cost and makes numbering byte-stable across email, TUI, and exports by construction.
RULING 2 — consolidated into ONE dependency gate for the user
Three lanes each surfaced 'Barkpark's first heavy external runtime' independently: server-side PDF generation (atlas investment #1; the trust professions' handed-over artifact), Typst/Verovio for publish-time notation snapshots (notation Rung 3), and the CDN client-engine question (is the mermaid pattern a blessed lane to extend with abcjs, or debt to retire?). These are ONE doctrine decision wearing three costumes: does Barkpark stay pure-twin/zero-runtime forever, or admit derived-render infrastructure? Recommendation: decide it once, deliberately — v1 ships on browser print + source badges (zero new dependencies, honest degrades); the derived-asset pipeline (PDF + notation snapshots, likely the same Chromium/Typst-shaped machinery behind the same sv-versioned snapshot pattern Sheets already proves) is opened as its own priced wave when a trust-artifact or science/music vertical is crowned. The CDN ruling is severable and cheap: the pattern is already codified in the CSP for mermaid + asciinema; blessing abcjs extends an existing lane, not a new posture.
  • Ratified: computed cells stay in sheets. The ~90-function engine is the one formula context; papers reference it via embeds and sheet-source chart/stat. A second formula context inside Papers means a second dependency graph, cycle detector, and parity surface — rejected for v1, with a narrow table total-row as a possible later exception (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms).
  • Ratified: the portability doctrine held everywhere. Every design in every lane renders on all three surfaces with honest degrades (box plot → five-number line; staff notation → metadata box + folded source; annotations → text summary in email). No web-only escape hatch survived review.
  • Ratified: every new block ships WITH its authoring surface. The editor census proves authoring, not rendering, is where features die — 12 S-tier blocks born unreachable. Palette entry + default_block clause + (where relevant) the shared source-editor node are part of a block's definition of done, permanently.

Risks and unknowns

  • Demand is inferred, not measured. All internal usage data is agent-authored; no human professional has ever been watched authoring a Paper. The crowns rest deliberately on external market evidence (TpT, the re-export loop, the Confluence exodus). Wave 1 is the cheap falsifiable test, and the flagship showcase Papers should double as the first instrumented measurement.
  • The teacher wedge must beat free. Google Forms is $0, district-mandated, and still improving (native close/caps landed Jan 2026 — demoted provenance, verify before scoping stage 6 against it). The wedge survives on what Forms cannot be: a beautiful printed artifact and a live form as ONE document, FERPA-safe by anonymity. This remains the least-grounded switching estimate in the program.
  • Feature-parity slippage is proven, not hypothetical. Chart annotations shipped web-only despite the type-parity gate — the gate locks types, not features. Every chart/form feature in waves 2-3 lands as a three-surface set with per-surface goldens, or the surfaces fork.
  • The parity treadmill on notation. Hand-growing a bounded TeX parser across three twins toward LaTeX-grade is parity-fragile. Mitigations: Temml as a frozen reference spec, golden parity at birth, and a hard scope line at the problem-set minimal set — beyond it, the honest answer is Rung 3's engine, not a bigger macro table.
  • Each new aggregate source re-opens privacy design. k-anon, measure whitelist, and tenancy checks were task-shaped by construction. form_responses is the easiest first source but still needs its own k-anonymity story.
  • The pitch must stay honest. 'Live' = refresh-on-save, not reader-side recompute; version history is professional-grade, never 'compliance'; email math stays a badge until the derived-asset gate opens. The quality-bar thesis dies the moment marketing outruns the render.
  • Concurrent-session hazard. The working tree provably lags origin/main; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic re-verifies the 33, the open task states, and PR-level facts at wave start — this repo moves daily.
  • Where does the individual professional permanently live? Playground workspaces carry a 48h TTL; the free cloud trial reaches a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the playground flag is cheap; deciding the durable home (TTL'd playground → claim? free papers-only tier? paid instance?) is a product decision outside this repo — without it, the toolkits polish a door with no house behind it.

The recommendation

GO — as a phased epic program, wave 1 first
The verdict is GO, with the two-layer shape rather than the wish's implicit build-blocks-per-profession shape. The evidence is unambiguous that the highest-leverage first wave is the door, not any new capability: it is the cheap half, it serves all twelve professions simultaneously, it has zero doctrine questions, and it falsifiably tests demand before the deeper waves spend. Then crown Teachers (wave 2) and Numbers-narrative (wave 3, engineers' template pack alongside), then the user-decided deep third crown (wave 4) whose evidence spine — the apparatus pass — serves lawyers and mathematicians regardless of the call. Run it as epic cycles per the standing rule; each wave above is one cycle with its charter drawn from this report and its lane Paper.

What the first wave takes, concretely: palette expansion with designed presets (the D4 decision record), default_block parity + the note/stage/card fix, the equation authoring rescue, compound-insert starters + cookbook links, markdown ingest wiring, pdd-t1 vertical template doc-types, the browser-print end-to-end proof, and the anonymous playground gate. Every item is anchored in §Files and carries no golden-regeneration debt except its own new fixtures.

The judgment calls that are yours
(1) THE DEEP THIRD CROWN: scientists/technical authors (evidence-favored) vs musicians (spectacle-favored) — the delight pack ships either way. (2) THE DEPENDENCY GATE (Ruling 2): may Barkpark ever run an external render runtime (PDF + notation snapshots), and is the CDN client-engine pattern blessed to extend (abcjs)? (3) WHERE THE PROFESSIONAL LIVES: TTL'd playground, a free papers-only tier, or the paid instance — the zero-setup promise cannot be met by any current route without this call. (4) INLINE MATH IN PROSE: commit in the notation second wave, or accept the adoption cap (every competitor has $..$; the mark vocabulary cost is real). (5) TEACHER SUB-SCOPE: K-12 printable culture first (recommended) vs higher-ed problem sets (needs equation v2 first). (6) THE HASH-CHAIN upgrade on revisions: cheap tamper-evidence vs the compliance-adjacent overclaim it invites. (7) RATIFY the toolkit anatomy and the pre-resolve ruling — both are this report's recommendations, not yet your law.

The paper stack — where to descend

This report stands alone, but every section compresses a lane Paper that holds the full depth: complete profession profiles and the regulatory matrix with controlling rules (papers-pro-toolkit-profession-atlas); the three-rung notation family with per-block attrs shapes, the engine census, and the competitor matrix (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting); the apparatus-pass architecture, the CSL/DOI design, the legal toolkit, and the record-integrity audit with trigger-level evidence (papers-pro-toolkit-evidence-record); the ranked chart-statistics pack, the six-stage form lifecycle, and the insert census (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms); the toolkit anatomy, the interop wall, the sequencing rationale, and the full coverage appendices (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit). Each lane's coverage appendix lists what was checked and NOT found — absences are decisions-in-waiting, and they are this program's sharpest evidence.

The one-sentence answer to the wish
What do the twelve professions need from Papers? A door they can walk through (palette, starters, import, playground), instruments that close their own loops (forms that grade, numbers that stay live), an apparatus that makes documents prove things (citations, numbering, records told honestly), notation that respects their craft (equations, chords) — all under one law: every block renders beautifully on web, email, and terminal. The engine is already most of the way there; this program's job is to open the door and set three flagship examples of the quality bar so high that the Papers sell Barkpark by themselves.

The wish, the frame, and how the investigation ran

The wish, verbatim in spirit: map what every named profession craves from Papers — musicians, data analysts, healthcare professionals, financial people, lawyers, mathematicians, scientists, industrial engineers, engineers in general, dentists, teachers — holistically, and build a toolkit so incredible that people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone. The interview pinned four frame-setting truths before the run launched, and every lane inherited them as law:

  • The buyer is an individual professional. A single dentist, teacher, or analyst picks Barkpark for their own documents. Consumer-grade onboarding, zero setup — the Paper IS the product.
  • The portability doctrine holds. Every new need becomes a new portable block type rendering on all three surfaces — web, email, terminal. No web-only escape hatches.
  • Map ALL, then crown 2–3. Every profession gets a profile; two or three highest-leverage verticals get deeply designed toolkits.
  • The quality bar itself is the attraction. In the user's own words: 'no focus on commercial — Papers should be so nice that people get attracted to Barkpark in general because the quality bar is so high.' This is a capability study, not a pricing exercise.

Five lanes cut the problem as a demand-meets-supply matrix: one lane owns every profession's demand so nobody falls through the cracks; three lanes own the capability spines the professions converge on; one lane owns engine ground truth, toolkit anatomy, and the crown verdict. Each published a full preparation Paper — this report takes their best material and stands alone; descend into a lane only for its full depth.

The finding that reorders everything

The engine kept growing; the door never did. Twelve S-tier blocks merged in one wave — and not one was added to the menu a human can see.

Every lane hit the same wall from a different direction, and the storm's editor census made it exact (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit carries the full census). The union of every human insert mechanism in the Studio editor — the 33-entry slash menu, the 25-type add-block dropdown, the 23-type canvas allowlist, the command palette — is exactly 33 of 75 classified block types. Not one instrument block is reachable: chart, stat, heatmap, form, questionnaire, sheet, and equation all have no insert path. The equation block shipped S-tier at usefulness 4.60 with three byte-identical surface twins and golden parity — and a mathematician cannot create one from the editor at all. Its graded source-textarea editor was never delivered either (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting).

This converts the corpus's most alarming number — 77.6% of 22,701 production blocks are bare paragraph + heading — from a demand signal into a supply artifact. The engine's own users, agents included, never reached the rich vocabulary because nothing offered it. The data-analyst notebook exists end-to-end today (sheet embed, live charts, write-through refresh) and has been used twice, ever. The anonymous form endpoint is live in prod with one real response — and the reader renders its form with no submit button, a door with no handle by explicit design (PR #5653 deferred the reader UI). The one-call playground that provisions a workspace, token, and seeded showcase Paper sits fully built behind a single require_admin flag, returning 401 to every stranger.

Three delivery-debt beliefs died under evidence along the way: the reader-CSS debt is PAID (PR #5651 shipped styling for all 18 previously-unstyled families); the TUI is NOT the weak parity leg (all 75 types have dedicated Go renderers — email is the constrained surface); and all 12 S-tier wishlist blocks are DONE. What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps — plus two verticals whose toolkits are ~90% shipped without anyone having assembled them, and the known capability gaps (math typesetting depth, citations, chart statistics, music) that sit exactly where professional cravings live.

The missing half is registry entries, default clauses, designed presets, starter templates, one controller branch, and one router pipeline. The cheapest wave in the whole program is also the one that serves all twelve professions at once, and it doubles as the falsifiable demand test: if lighting the door doesn't move usage, re-examine before building deeper (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms, Move 0).

Spine 3 · Evidence and record (lawyers, scientists, clinicians, financial)

One document-level apparatus pass plus a small block/mark family — completion, not invention. Full design: the evidence lane Paper.

REFERENCES
First-class type:'reference' documents storing CSL-JSON snapshots. Imported by a single zero-key DOI GET (live-proven against doi.org). Forced by the schema: content_edges' to_id must be a real document — which is exactly what buys the 'cited by' reverse view on the reader's existing backlinks machinery, plus a personal library a scientist will recognize as Zotero-lite.

Resolves cite marks (with the locator/pin-cite field no personal tool models — the wedge), derives the bibliography in a bounded five-style CSL formatter (APA, Vancouver, IEEE, Chicago, Harvard; honest degrade; never an open citeproc engine; Bluebook honestly declared un-servable), numbers figures/tables/equations/clauses/theorems, resolves crossrefs into human labels, completes footnote's inline half, and retrofits heading anchors — walk.ex emits zero id attributes in 1,565 lines today, so cross-references are broken at BOTH ends.
LEGAL V1

Say it exactly as honestly as the code allows Real DB triggers guard revisions against direct tampering — say 'professional-grade version history'. Workspace deletion cascades history away by design and mutation_events is unguarded — never say 'compliance'.

Spine 4 · Notation (mathematicians, scientists, engineers, teachers, musicians)

Grow the twins, don't buy an engine — the three-rung family, priced, lives in the notation lane Paper.

  1. Rung 1 — build-ready, zero dependencies

    The equation authoring rescue first: slash entry, canvas allowlist, default_block clause, the never-delivered source-textarea editor, $$ markdown ingestion. Then grammar v2 against Temml as a frozen reference spec — fix \sqrt (today a bare glyph that cannot wrap an argument), add nth-root, \text{}, mtable matrices/cases and aligned derivations, all MathML-Core-native — plus the first document-scope numbering pass, which no engine can provide (MathML Core excludes mlabeledtr; numbering is structurally Barkpark-side work, landing in the same apparatus pass as Spine 3). And the text-native musician family — chord-chart (ChordPro), tab, setlist, audio — where the TUI is the BEST surface, email is trivially safe, and the transpose algorithm is ~100 lines reimplemented MIT-clean (ChordSheetJS is GPL-2.0; reference only).

  2. Rung 2 — one script tag, CDN-gated

    An abc-notation staff-engraving block riding the exact CDN pattern mermaid uses today (abcjs, MIT, 148 KB gzip, host already CSP-whitelisted) — gated on the user's CDN ruling.

  3. Rung 3 — held, not defaulted

    Publish-time SVG/PNG snapshots per the Sheets sv-versioned pattern via Barkpark's FIRST external render runtime (Typst or Verovio) — the only path to publication-fidelity email math. Opened only if a science/music crown lands AND the user accepts the dependency.

The economics and the category move One shared type-parameterized source-textarea editor node (equation, abc, chord, tab all edit the same way) replaces ~514 lines of editor code per block. Native numbered equations + cross-references in a zero-setup tool is a category move — Notion's, Obsidian's, and GitBook's confirmed shared dead zone. Chemistry stays deferred (C-tier 1.55; smiles-drawer noted as the only CDN-viable escape hatch).

Doctrine rulings

Three questions no lane could settle alone were flagged to this capstone. Two are ruled here with reasoning; one is consolidated into a single user gate.

RULING 1 — Resolve-at-render, never-at-rest (the pre-resolve doctrine) The question, asked identically by three lanes: must every surface render from source, or may the server pre-resolve (citation formatting, numbering, freshness stamps, notation snapshots)? RULING: the server MAY pre-resolve, and derived document-level content SHOULD flow through one canonical Elixir resolver — because the system already does exactly this, safely, at scale. TaskResolver's resolve/2 + preview/2 split serves all six render call sites (web reader, live re-resolve, email snapshot-at-send, source endpoint, ?resolve= for the TUI, Studio preview) and never persists a resolved row; stored blocks stay byte-stable source, which is what the canvas diff and the golden harness actually require. The law is a two-line rule: SOURCE-level rendering (an equation's glyphs, a chord line, a chart's pixels) = three surface twins, byte-identical grammar. DOCUMENT-level derivation (bibliography text, assigned numbers, resolved labels, as-of stamps) = ONE resolver, all surfaces consume its output. Consequences: the apparatus pass is a new resolver in TaskResolver's shape; the CSL formatter is written once in Elixir (not three twins); freshness stamps are resolver chrome and legal; equation grammar v2 stays three-twin because equations render from source on every surface. This halves the evidence spine's cost and makes numbering byte-stable across email, TUI, and exports by construction.
RULING 2 — consolidated into ONE dependency gate for the user Three lanes each surfaced 'Barkpark's first heavy external runtime' independently: server-side PDF generation (atlas investment #1; the trust professions' handed-over artifact), Typst/Verovio for publish-time notation snapshots (notation Rung 3), and the CDN client-engine question (is the mermaid pattern a blessed lane to extend with abcjs, or debt to retire?). These are ONE doctrine decision wearing three costumes: does Barkpark stay pure-twin/zero-runtime forever, or admit derived-render infrastructure? Recommendation: decide it once, deliberately — v1 ships on browser print + source badges (zero new dependencies, honest degrades); the derived-asset pipeline (PDF + notation snapshots, likely the same Chromium/Typst-shaped machinery behind the same sv-versioned snapshot pattern Sheets already proves) is opened as its own priced wave when a trust-artifact or science/music vertical is crowned. The CDN ruling is severable and cheap: the pattern is already codified in the CSP for mermaid + asciinema; blessing abcjs extends an existing lane, not a new posture.
  • Ratified: computed cells stay in sheets. The ~90-function engine is the one formula context; papers reference it via embeds and sheet-source chart/stat. A second formula context inside Papers means a second dependency graph, cycle detector, and parity surface — rejected for v1, with a narrow table total-row as a possible later exception (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms).
  • Ratified: the portability doctrine held everywhere. Every design in every lane renders on all three surfaces with honest degrades (box plot → five-number line; staff notation → metadata box + folded source; annotations → text summary in email). No web-only escape hatch survived review.
  • Ratified: every new block ships WITH its authoring surface. The editor census proves authoring, not rendering, is where features die — 12 S-tier blocks born unreachable. Palette entry + default_block clause + (where relevant) the shared source-editor node are part of a block's definition of done, permanently.

Risks and unknowns

  • Demand is inferred, not measured. All internal usage data is agent-authored; no human professional has ever been watched authoring a Paper. The crowns rest deliberately on external market evidence (TpT, the re-export loop, the Confluence exodus). Wave 1 is the cheap falsifiable test, and the flagship showcase Papers should double as the first instrumented measurement.
  • The teacher wedge must beat free. Google Forms is $0, district-mandated, and still improving (native close/caps landed Jan 2026 — demoted provenance, verify before scoping stage 6 against it). The wedge survives on what Forms cannot be: a beautiful printed artifact and a live form as ONE document, FERPA-safe by anonymity. This remains the least-grounded switching estimate in the program.
  • Feature-parity slippage is proven, not hypothetical. Chart annotations shipped web-only despite the type-parity gate — the gate locks types, not features. Every chart/form feature in waves 2-3 lands as a three-surface set with per-surface goldens, or the surfaces fork.
  • The parity treadmill on notation. Hand-growing a bounded TeX parser across three twins toward LaTeX-grade is parity-fragile. Mitigations: Temml as a frozen reference spec, golden parity at birth, and a hard scope line at the problem-set minimal set — beyond it, the honest answer is Rung 3's engine, not a bigger macro table.
  • Each new aggregate source re-opens privacy design. k-anon, measure whitelist, and tenancy checks were task-shaped by construction. form_responses is the easiest first source but still needs its own k-anonymity story.
  • The pitch must stay honest. 'Live' = refresh-on-save, not reader-side recompute; version history is professional-grade, never 'compliance'; email math stays a badge until the derived-asset gate opens. The quality-bar thesis dies the moment marketing outruns the render.
  • Concurrent-session hazard. The working tree provably lags origin/main; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic re-verifies the 33, the open task states, and PR-level facts at wave start — this repo moves daily.
  • Where does the individual professional permanently live? Playground workspaces carry a 48h TTL; the free cloud trial reaches a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the playground flag is cheap; deciding the durable home (TTL'd playground → claim? free papers-only tier? paid instance?) is a product decision outside this repo — without it, the toolkits polish a door with no house behind it.

The recommendation

GO — as a phased epic program, wave 1 first The verdict is GO, with the two-layer shape rather than the wish's implicit build-blocks-per-profession shape. The evidence is unambiguous that the highest-leverage first wave is the door, not any new capability: it is the cheap half, it serves all twelve professions simultaneously, it has zero doctrine questions, and it falsifiably tests demand before the deeper waves spend. Then crown Teachers (wave 2) and Numbers-narrative (wave 3, engineers' template pack alongside), then the user-decided deep third crown (wave 4) whose evidence spine — the apparatus pass — serves lawyers and mathematicians regardless of the call. Run it as epic cycles per the standing rule; each wave above is one cycle with its charter drawn from this report and its lane Paper.

What the first wave takes, concretely: palette expansion with designed presets (the D4 decision record), default_block parity + the note/stage/card fix, the equation authoring rescue, compound-insert starters + cookbook links, markdown ingest wiring, pdd-t1 vertical template doc-types, the browser-print end-to-end proof, and the anonymous playground gate. Every item is anchored in §Files and carries no golden-regeneration debt except its own new fixtures.

The judgment calls that are yours (1) THE DEEP THIRD CROWN: scientists/technical authors (evidence-favored) vs musicians (spectacle-favored) — the delight pack ships either way. (2) THE DEPENDENCY GATE (Ruling 2): may Barkpark ever run an external render runtime (PDF + notation snapshots), and is the CDN client-engine pattern blessed to extend (abcjs)? (3) WHERE THE PROFESSIONAL LIVES: TTL'd playground, a free papers-only tier, or the paid instance — the zero-setup promise cannot be met by any current route without this call. (4) INLINE MATH IN PROSE: commit in the notation second wave, or accept the adoption cap (every competitor has $..$; the mark vocabulary cost is real). (5) TEACHER SUB-SCOPE: K-12 printable culture first (recommended) vs higher-ed problem sets (needs equation v2 first). (6) THE HASH-CHAIN upgrade on revisions: cheap tamper-evidence vs the compliance-adjacent overclaim it invites. (7) RATIFY the toolkit anatomy and the pre-resolve ruling — both are this report's recommendations, not yet your law.

The paper stack — where to descend

This report stands alone, but every section compresses a lane Paper that holds the full depth: complete profession profiles and the regulatory matrix with controlling rules (papers-pro-toolkit-profession-atlas); the three-rung notation family with per-block attrs shapes, the engine census, and the competitor matrix (papers-pro-toolkit-notation-typesetting); the apparatus-pass architecture, the CSL/DOI design, the legal toolkit, and the record-integrity audit with trigger-level evidence (papers-pro-toolkit-evidence-record); the ranked chart-statistics pack, the six-stage form lifecycle, and the insert census (papers-pro-toolkit-living-data-forms); the toolkit anatomy, the interop wall, the sequencing rationale, and the full coverage appendices (papers-pro-toolkit-crown-and-toolkit). Each lane's coverage appendix lists what was checked and NOT found — absences are decisions-in-waiting, and they are this program's sharpest evidence.

The one-sentence answer to the wish What do the twelve professions need from Papers? A door they can walk through (palette, starters, import, playground), instruments that close their own loops (forms that grade, numbers that stay live), an apparatus that makes documents prove things (citations, numbering, records told honestly), notation that respects their craft (equations, chords) — all under one law: every block renders beautifully on web, email, and terminal. The engine is already most of the way there; this program's job is to open the door and set three flagship examples of the quality bar so high that the Papers sell Barkpark by themselves.
